laws of the United States of America, including sections 212(f) and 215(a)(1) 
of the Immigration and Nationality Act, as amended (8 U.S.C. 1182(f) and 
1185(a)(1)), and section 301 of title 3, United States Code, and in order 
to delegate appropriate responsibilities to Federal agencies for responding 
to migration of undocumented aliens in the Caribbean region, it is hereby 
ordered:

clauses.label: Section 1.
clauses.text:

and operate a facility, or facilities, to house and provide for the needs 
of any such aliens. Such a facility may be located at Guantanamo Bay 
Naval Base or any other appropriate location.

clauses.label: (ii)
clauses.text:
(ii) The Attorney General may conduct any screening of such aliens that 
he deems appropriate, including screening to determine whether such aliens 
should be returned to their country of origin or transit, or whether they 
are persons in need of protection who should not be returned without 
their consent. If the Attorney General institutes such screening, then until 
a determination is made, the Attorney General shall provide for the custody, 
care, safety, transportation, and other needs of the aliens. The Attorney 
General shall continue to provide for the custody, care, safety, transportation, 
and other needs of aliens who are determined not to be persons in need 
of protection until such time as they are returned to their country of origin 
or transit.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) The Secretary of State shall provide for the custody, care, safety, 
transportation, and other needs of undocumented aliens interdicted or inter-
cepted in the Caribbean region whom the Attorney General has identified 
as persons in need of protection. The Secretary of State shall provide for 
and execute a process for resettling such persons in need of protection, 
as appropriate, in countries other than their country of origin, and shall 
also undertake such diplomatic efforts as may be necessary to address the 
problem of illegal migration of aliens in the Caribbean region and to facilitate 
the return of those aliens who are determined not to be persons in need 
of protection.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:

sible for reimbursement for necessary supporting utilities.

(ii) In the event of a mass migration in the Caribbean region, the Secretary

versions.research_rationale:
Executive Order 13276 of November 15, 2002 (67 FR 69985), Delegation of Responsibilities Concerning Undocumented Aliens Interdicted or Intercepted in the Caribbean Region, issued under sections 212(f) and 215(a)(1) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1182(f), 1185(a)(1)) and 3 U.S.C. 301, assigns duties for undocumented aliens interdicted in the Caribbean region: section 1(a) custody and screening (originally the Attorney General) with a facility possibly at Guantanamo Bay, 1(b) the Secretary of State on persons in need of protection and resettlement, 1(c) the Secretary of Defense on facilities and, in a mass migration, support; section 2 defines mass migration; section 3 contains scope and general provisions. The 14-clause machine inventory covers the whole text from the preamble to section 3(e) and I confirmed it is complete; the entries 'lead' (the authority recital), 'sec1' (the lead-in to section 1) and 'sec3' (the heading of the scope section) are not commands but frame the commands and are carried as operative with the order. The one amending order found is EO 13286 (February 28, 2003, effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92), section 1, which replaces the Attorney General with the Secretary of Homeland Security wherever it appears in section 1; the OFR catalog record for EO 13276 lists no 'Amended by' note and instead reads 'See: EO 12807, May 24, 1992 | Amends: EO 13286, February 28, 2003'; EO 13286 was signed after EO 13276 and its section 1 amends EO 13276, so I read that catalog note as a transposed record of the EO 13286 amendment, not as a second instrument. EO 12807 (Interdiction of Illegal Aliens) is referred to in sections 1(c)(ii) and 3(a) and is not a revocation or amendment of this order. Search of held texts for the number EO 13276 finds the order, EO 13286, the Federal Register copies of those two, 32 CFR 245.9 (which lists EO 13286 as amending EO 13276), two Federal Register copies of Cuba-policy presidential memoranda (the National Security Presidential Memorandum published at 82 FR 48875, October 20, 2017, and the Memorandum of June 30, 2025, 90 FR 38913) that each state they do not affect EO 13276; none revokes or supersedes the order. The bounded searches report no machine hit that ends it. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. The 8 U.S.C. 1182 note prints the order as amended. The order's own text has no end date; the 'until' phrases in section 1(a)(ii) set how long the custody duty lasts for a particular alien, not an end of the clause. The order is operative as of 2026-10-14.

versions.research_rationale:
Executive Order 13276 of November 15, 2002 (67 FR 69985), Delegation of Responsibilities Concerning Undocumented Aliens Interdicted or Intercepted in the Caribbean Region, issued under sections 212(f) and 215(a)(1) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1182(f), 1185(a)(1)) and 3 U.S.C. 301, assigns duties for undocumented aliens interdicted in the Caribbean region: section 1(a) custody and screening (originally the Attorney General) with a facility possibly at Guantanamo Bay, 1(b) the Secretary of State on persons in need of protection and resettlement, 1(c) the Secretary of Defense on facilities and, in a mass migration, support; section 2 defines mass migration; section 3 contains scope and general provisions. The 14-clause machine inventory covers the whole text from the preamble to section 3(e) and I confirmed it is complete; I corrected it to 13 clauses by merging the 14-character section 3 heading into section 3(a), and the entries 'lead' (the authority recital) and 'sec1' (the lead-in to section 1) are not commands but frame the commands and are carried as operative with the order. The one amending order found is EO 13286 (February 28, 2003, effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92), section 1, which replaces the Attorney General with the Secretary of Homeland Security wherever it appears in section 1; the OFR catalog record for EO 13276 lists no 'Amended by' note and instead reads 'See: EO 12807, May 24, 1992 | Amends: EO 13286, February 28, 2003'; EO 13286 was signed after EO 13276 and its section 1 amends EO 13276, so I read that catalog note as a transposed record of the EO 13286 amendment, not as a second instrument. EO 12807 (Interdiction of Illegal Aliens) is referred to in sections 1(c)(ii) and 3(a) and is not a revocation or amendment of this order. Search of held texts for the number EO 13276 finds the order, EO 13286, the Federal Register copies of those two, 32 CFR 245.9 (which lists EO 13286 as amending EO 13276), two Federal Register copies of Cuba-policy presidential memoranda (the National Security Presidential Memorandum published at 82 FR 48875, October 20, 2017, and the Memorandum of June 30, 2025, 90 FR 38913) that each state they do not affect EO 13276; none revokes or supersedes the order. The bounded searches report no machine hit that ends it. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. The 8 U.S.C. 1182 note prints the order as amended. The order's own text has no end date; the 'until' phrases in section 1(a)(ii) set how long the custody duty lasts for a particular alien, not an end of the clause. The order is operative as of 2026-10-14.

versions.research_rationale:
Executive Order 13276 of November 15, 2002 (67 FR 69985), Delegation of Responsibilities Concerning Undocumented Aliens Interdicted or Intercepted in the Caribbean Region, issued under sections 212(f) and 215(a)(1) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1182(f), 1185(a)(1)) and 3 U.S.C. 301, assigns duties for undocumented aliens interdicted in the Caribbean region: section 1(a) custody and screening (originally the Attorney General) with a facility possibly at Guantanamo Bay, 1(b) the Secretary of State on persons in need of protection and resettlement, 1(c) the Secretary of Defense on facilities and, in a mass migration, support; section 2 defines mass migration; section 3 contains scope and general provisions. The 14-clause machine inventory covers the whole text from the preamble to section 3(e) and I confirmed it is complete; I corrected it to 13 clauses by merging the 14-character section 3 heading into section 3(a), and the entries 'lead' (the authority recital) and 'sec1' (the lead-in to section 1) are not commands but frame the commands and are carried as operative with the order. The one amending order found is EO 13286 (February 28, 2003, effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92), section 1, which replaces the Attorney General with the Secretary of Homeland Security wherever it appears in section 1; the OFR catalog record for EO 13276 lists no 'Amended by' note and instead reads 'See: EO 12807, May 24, 1992 | Amends: EO 13286, February 28, 2003'; EO 13286 was signed after EO 13276 and its section 1 amends EO 13276, so I read that catalog note as a transposed record of the EO 13286 amendment, not as a second instrument. EO 12807 (Interdiction of Illegal Aliens) is referred to in sections 1(c)(ii) and 3(a) and is not a revocation or amendment of this order. Search of held texts for the number EO 13276 finds the order, EO 13286, the Federal Register copies of those two, 32 CFR 245.9 (which lists EO 13286 as amending EO 13276), two Federal Register copies of Cuba-policy presidential memoranda (the National Security Presidential Memorandum published at 82 FR 48875, October 20, 2017, and the Memorandum of June 30, 2025, 90 FR 38913) that each state they do not affect EO 13276; none revokes or supersedes the order. The bounded searches report machine hits (the OFR catalog entries, the text of EO 13286 and the U.S. Code note), none of which revokes, supersedes or ends the order. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. The 8 U.S.C. 1182 note prints the order as amended. The order's own text has no end date; the 'until' phrases in section 1(a)(ii) set how long the custody duty lasts for a particular alien, not an end of the clause. The order is operative as of 2026-10-14.
